{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Inspect the data
print("Shape:", df.shape)
print("\nColumns:", df.columns.tolist())
print("\nUnique customer_segment values:", df['customer_segment'].unique().tolist())
print("\nCustomer_segment counts:\n", df['customer_segment'].value_counts().sort_index())

# Check for the presence of 'loyal' customers
has_loyal = 'loyal' in df['customer_segment'].unique()

# Check the 'converted' column
print("\nConverted column unique values:", df['converted'].unique())
print("Converted column value counts:\n", df['converted'].value_counts().sort_index())

# Check for sentinel values in customer_age
print("\nNumber of customer_age == -1:", (df['customer_age'] == -1).sum())

# Check revenue column: string with commas?
print("\nFirst 5 revenue values:", df['revenue'].head().tolist())
print("Revenue dtype:", df['revenue'].dtype)

# Check for QA orders (revenue = 999999.99)
print("\nNumber of rows with revenue == 999999.99:", (df['revenue'] == '999999.99').sum())

# Check for refunded orders
print("\nStatus counts:\n", df['status'].value_counts())

# Final check: are there any rows with 'loyal'?
loyal_rows = df[df['customer_segment'] == 'loyal']
print("\nNumber of loyal customer rows:", len(loyal_rows))

# Return the loyal rows to check converted
loyal_converted = loyal_rows['converted'].value_counts().sort_index()
print("\nConverted in loyal segment:\n", loyal_converted)

# Return the result
loyal_converted.get(1, 0) / len(loyal_rows)"}
